result.title: When Do Spatial Plans Help Text-to-Image Generation? Causal Control, System Utility, and Text Responsiveness
result.summary: A generator can follow a spatial plan, but the benefit of supplying that plan depends on what the model can already do from text. In a controlled study with 18 paired training seeds, correcting predicted positions and sizes improves spatial intersection-over-union by 0.030, yet direct text is non-inferior at matched training compute. In a pretrained generator, a fixed rule layout improves two-object task success over the same text-only adapter by 12.50 percentage points, mostly by separating objects that already appear in the correct order. We then ask whether a more precise instruction can achieve the same separation across conditioning paths. On 288 new task families, adding a minimum-gap instruction improves success by 37.15 points with the text-only adapter, by at most 0.69 points with widely spaced regions, and by 6.94 points with tightly spaced regions. Under tight regions, 230 of 288 baseline images have the correct objects and direction yet miss the required gap, ruling out a high baseline success rate as the sole explanation for the weak text response.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过控制实验考察文本到图像生成中额外空间布局条件是否真正带来收益：在 18 组配对训练种子上纠正预测位置与尺寸，并在匹配训练算力下与纯文本条件比较；在预训练生成器上比较固定规则布局与文本适配器，再用最小间距指令检验不同条件路径对文本的响应程度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其因果纠正、匹配算力对照以及排除基线饱和的解释方式，可能为判断 LVR 中额外 latent 状态是否被实际使用、收益归因与条件路径冗余提供可核查的方法线索，但任务为图像生成，缺少显式推理状态。
